decisions.reason: Because it has survived its first market test and supports the firm's digital efficiency agenda, management would likely keep it, though after two years any sales below aspiration could start to raise pressure to reallocate resources.

The web tool is cheap and complementary to engineering work, so slack supports retention, but as a narrow niche offering it remains the most exposed if usage and project pull stay below aspiration levels.

This product fits the firm's established solution business and customer efficiency needs, so it is likely to be retained unless its results now clearly lag both internal expectations and comparable firms' outcomes.

As a close extension of the hydraulic infrastructure portfolio, it would usually be given more time in project-based markets, though a weaker strategic fit than the firm's digital products makes withdrawal somewhat more conceivable.

The energy management system is highly consistent with the firm's stated direction toward intelligent, efficient and environmentally beneficial infrastructure control, making continued support very likely.
A dedicated product line with several models signals commitment and portfolio relevance, so an expanding firm would normally keep it unless early demand falls materially short of aspirations.
